Versico: The Value Line for Straightforward Single-Ply Jobs

Versico operates under the same parent company as Carlisle SynTec, sharing manufacturing infrastructure while running as a separate brand positioned toward more budget-conscious commercial roofing projects. On a straightforward warehouse or retail roof without unusual exposure conditions or complex geometry, Versico often produces the tightest bid among comparable single-ply options without sacrificing warranty depth on the specs owners actually need.

What We Install From the Versico Line

Versico's TPO membrane covers the standard thickness range detailed on our 60-mil and 80-mil TPO pages, in mechanically attached, fully adhered, and induction-welded configurations. Their PVC line covers the same territory detailed on our PVC roof systems page for buildings with grease or chemical exposure where that chemistry fits better than TPO. Both product families are manufactured to compete on price against the more established brand names in the same corporate family, while still carrying comparable no-dollar-limit warranty programs.

We do not treat Versico as a compromise choice. On a clean, open-field logistics roof with no unusual exposure or geometry, the membrane chemistry and installation methods are the same regardless of brand, and a Versico bid frequently lands lower without giving up thickness, attachment method, or warranty term compared to the more recognized name-brand alternative. Sharing manufacturing infrastructure with Carlisle also means Versico's material lead times generally track the same regional supply chain, so choosing the value line rarely means waiting longer for membrane to reach the jobsite.

Where This Fits Ontario's Building Stock

We spec Versico most often on spec-built warehouse and distribution buildings in the Ontario Ranch and Meredith International Centre submarkets, where the owner's pro forma assumes a shorter hold period and the pressure on first cost is real. It also shows up regularly on multi-tenant retail strip reroofs across the market, where the roof area per tenant space is modest and every line item on the bid gets scrutinized against the property's operating budget. Older light-industrial buildings around Jurupa Valley and Mira Loma's historic warehouse district are a similar case, where the roof simply needs to perform for its remaining useful life without the owner paying for warranty years the building will not see.

Warranty Structure

Versico's no-dollar-limit warranties follow the same industry-standard bands as other manufacturers in this price tier, typically 15 to 20 years, scaled to membrane thickness and installation detail quality. The warranty documentation and manufacturer inspection process mirror what we run on any major manufacturer's job — there is no shortcut on closeout inspection just because the material cost came in lower. The owner's maintenance obligation over the warranty term — clear drains, sound seams, prompt repair of accidental damage — is identical to what any other manufacturer's program requires, and we document it the same way regardless of which brand is on the roof.

  • Product lines available: TPO (60 and 80 mil), PVC (50 to 80 mil)
  • Attachment methods: mechanically attached, fully adhered, induction-welded
  • Warranty terms: typically 15 to 20 years NDL, scaled to thickness and detail quality
  • Pricing position: generally the lower-cost option within a shared corporate manufacturing base with Carlisle SynTec
  • Best-fit buildings: spec-built warehouse and distribution roofs, multi-tenant retail strip reroofs, short-hold ownership periods
  • Closeout process: manufacturer inspection required before warranty issuance, same as any major manufacturer program

How We Weigh Versico Against Other Manufacturers

For a straightforward job with standard conditions, we put Versico's bid next to the more recognized name-brand alternatives and let material cost, current lead time, and warranty term settle the choice. Where we steer away from Versico is on jobs with complex existing conditions, unusual chemical exposure, or an institutional owner whose lender specifically wants a particular manufacturer's name on the warranty documentation for underwriting reasons unrelated to the roof's actual performance. On a merchant-built spec warehouse with a straightforward open field and a 10-year hold in the pro forma, none of those factors apply, and the lower material cost goes straight to the bottom line without giving up anything the owner will actually use.

Common Questions on Versico Roofing

Is Versico lower quality than Carlisle since it's the budget line?

The membrane chemistry and manufacturing standards are consistent within the shared corporate structure; the pricing difference reflects market positioning more than a material quality gap. For standard installation conditions, the products perform comparably.

Does a Versico warranty hold up the same as a more recognized brand's warranty?

The warranty terms and administration process follow the same industry-standard structure, including manufacturer inspection before issuance. Some institutional lenders have brand preferences unrelated to actual roof performance, which is worth checking before finalizing a manufacturer choice on a financed project.

When would you recommend against Versico?

On jobs with complex existing roof conditions, documented chemical exposure needing a specialty PVC formulation, or where an owner's lender specifically requires a different manufacturer's name for underwriting purposes.

Is Versico TPO the same product as Carlisle TPO with a different label?

The two brands are manufactured within the same parent company but are formulated and marketed as distinct product lines with their own specifications and warranty programs, not identical products under two names.

Can Versico products be mixed with Carlisle products on the same roof?

We generally keep a single manufacturer's warranty program on one continuous roof area to avoid complicating the warranty documentation, even though the two brands share a parent company. Separate roof sections or buildings can use different manufacturers without issue.
